subject.title: resolveCliAuthEpoch invalidates every live CLI session when local credential source-of-storage flips, even though identity is unchanged

question: Should Claude CLI reusable-session auth epochs track stable credential identity rather than local credential storage/source shape when an OpenClaw auth profile is also present?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the safe fix depends on a maintainer-owned auth boundary: OpenClaw must avoid spurious resets without accidentally reusing a CLI session across a real or unprovable credential identity change.

options.title: Use Identity-Stable, Fail-Closed Claude CLI Epochs
options.body: Implement an internal Claude CLI policy that ignores storage-source presence only when identity equivalence is proven, and resets when identity is absent or ambiguous.

options.title: Adopt Host-Owned Claude CLI Epochs
options.body: Accept the host CLI credential as the session owner for Claude CLI and resolve the overlapping PR direction with explicit security and upgrade proof.

options.title: Keep Current Fail-Closed Behavior
options.body: Leave source-presence changes as invalidating and document mitigation for users who share Claude Code credentials with OpenClaw.

recommendation.title: Use Identity-Stable, Fail-Closed Claude CLI Epochs
recommendation.body: Implement an internal Claude CLI policy that ignores storage-source presence only when identity equivalence is proven, and resets when identity is absent or ambiguous.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history on CLI OAuth session continuity and the affected session/auth surfaces.
